steps.body: Fourteen, fifteen, sixteen say their secret out loud: FOUR-teen, FIF-teen, SIX-teen — the ones first, then “teen” for the ten.
steps.narration: Fourteen, fifteen, sixteen say their secret out loud: FOUR-teen, FIF-teen, SIX-teen — the ones first, then “teen” for the ten.

widget.prompt: A carton already holds ten muffins. Add loose muffins until the tray holds 14 in all.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 loose muffins leaves 4 still missing — ten alone is only 10, not 14.
3 loose muffins leaves 1 still missing; ten and 3 is 13, one short of 14.
5 loose muffins adds 1 too many; ten and 5 is 15, one past 14.

widget.missFeedback: The ten muffins are done; keep adding loose ones until the tray holds 14.
widget.successFeedback: 14 muffins — one full carton of ten, plus 4 more loose ones.

predict.prompt: What does the “four” in fourteen count?

options.label: The four ones past the ten

predict.reveal: The -teen ending carries the ten; the front of the word counts only the extras.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb 14 16.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb 14 16 rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: A model shows one full ten and six loose dots. Build the loose part of 16.

7 adds 1 too many; ten and 7 is 17, one past 16.

widget.missFeedback: The ten is done; count on from 10 while adding dots, and stop when you reach 16.
widget.successFeedback: 16 built — one complete ten and 6 more, exactly what the teen numeral says.

widget.prompt: What does the numeral 15 secretly say?

options.label: One complete ten, and five more
options.feedback: Correct — the 1 stands for a whole ten, the 5 for the ones riding on top.

options.label: A one and a five, side by side
options.feedback: That reads the digits as neighbours; the left digit is a whole TEN, not a one.

options.label: Five tens and a one
options.feedback: That swaps the digits' jobs — the ten is on the left, the ones on the right.

options.label: Fifteen separate tens
options.feedback: Only the single left digit counts tens; fifteen has exactly one of them.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 5. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 14 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 15.
16 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 5 hops from 10 to land on 15.

widget.missFeedback: Count 5 on from 10: you land on 15.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 5 more is 15 — the teen numeral written as a walk: ten first, then the ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 5 counts past ten are needed to reach 15.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 5 numbers, on 15.
